examples.subject: Your New Travel Portal — Making Payments Easy & Secure
examples.body:
Hi John and Missy,

I wanted to reach out personally because I've been working on
something that's going to make your life a whole lot easier when it
comes to managing your upcoming trip.

I've recently set up a secure Client Travel Portal through our booking
management system. Think of it as your own private dashboard for
everything related to your trip — your itinerary, your documents, your
invoices, and most importantly, a safe and simple way to handle
payments.

Here's what's coming your way over the next day or so:

STEP 1: You'll receive a Portal Activation email from Dreams2Memories Travel.
  • Click the "Activate Now" button in that email
  • You can set up your login two ways:
      - Passkey (recommended) — one-tap login, no codes to remember
      - One-Time Email Code — a unique code sent to your email each
time you sign in
  • The activation link expires in 24 hours, so please set it up when you see it

STEP 2: Once you're in, you'll receive an Invoice email.
  • This will have a detailed breakdown of your trip costs, payment
schedule, and what's due
  • You can also view this invoice anytime inside your portal

STEP 3: Add your credit card securely through the portal.
  • Inside the portal, you'll see an option to add a payment method
  • Your card information is encrypted and stored securely — I never
see your full card number in plain text
  • This is the same secure system used by thousands of travel agents
and their clients nationwide
  • Please do NOT email credit card numbers — the portal is the safe
way to do this

Once your card is on file, I can process your payments on schedule
without having to chase anyone down by phone. You'll be able to see
your payment status, upcoming due dates, and trip details all in one
place.

Your trip: Regent Seven Seas Grandeur, Scandinavia, Aug 29, 2026
Final payment due: April 1, 2026

If you run into any issues activating your portal or have questions
about the invoice, just call me or shoot me a text. I'm always here.

Looking forward to this trip with you — it's going to be an incredible
experience.

Thanks,
John

John Loucks
Dreams2Memories Travel, LLC

johnloucks3@gmail.com

upcoming Denver trip and send it along to both of you — so here it is, hot
off the wire.

✈️ DCA → DEN | Jul 18–25, 2026 | 4 Passengers

examples.subject: Re: What Organized Travel Actually Looks Like
examples.body: Hi Missy, Following up on the seat assignments for your outbound flights — I promised I'd come back to you, and here's where we are. What We Did John and I researched Finnair's seat selection policies for your Business Class flights and attempted to secure specific seats on your behalf. Because your booking originates through American Airlines (AA confirmation CKZHXA) but the flights are operated by Finnair (confirmation BB4X94), seat selection has to be done directly through Finnair's system — AA's system can't assign seats on Finnair-operated flights in advance. What's Available Your Business Class is fully guaranteed on both legs — that hasn't changed. Finnair flies the A350 on the DFW–Helsinki route, which has a 1-2-1 Business Class layout — every seat has direct aisle access. These are excellent seats no matter where you end up, but if you have a preference (window-side, certain row), you can lock that in now. How to Select Your Seats — Step by Step It takes about 3 minutes: 1. Go to finnair.com and click "Manage booking" (top right) 2. Enter your Finnair confirmation code: BB4X94 3. Enter last name: FURLOW 4. Once you're in, look for "Seat selection" or "Choose seats" 5. You'll see the seat map for each flight: — Aug 26: AA 9018 (Finnair operated) DFW → Helsinki — Aug 27: AY 811 Helsinki → Stockholm 6. Pick two seats for each leg (one for you, one for John) 7. Confirm your selections A few tips: - Business Class seat selection on Finnair is typically included at no extra charge for your fare class - On the A350, rows 1–6 are Business Class in a 1-2-1 "throne" configuration — window seats (A and K) offer the most privacy, middle pairs (D and G) are great for couples who want to be next to each other - If prompted for any fees, stop and let me know — that would mean the system is reading the fare class differently and I'll sort it out If you'd prefer not to deal with it, no problem at all — just let me know and John and I will find another way to get it done. We wanted to give you the option since it's quick and you'll get first pick of whatever's open. I have notified John, he is aware and he and I will be working the problem. Looking forward to connecting with you! Dani — Dani Moreau Luxury Travel Concierge Dreams2Memories Travel concierge@d2mluxury.quest

examples.subject: Mobility Scooter Rentals for Your Silver Nova Voyage — A Helpful Resource

DREAMS2MEMORIES

Curating the Voyage of Your Lifetime

Hi Ron,

I hope this message finds you well! I wanted to share a resource that may
be useful as you and Lindy prepare for your *Silversea Silver Nova* voyage
to Japan this April.

Whether you're planning ahead or just want to know your options, there are
dedicated mobility scooter and wheelchair rental services that work
directly with cruise lines — including Silversea. They handle everything:
delivery to your cabin, embarkation and debarkation logistics, and even
availability at select ports of call.

✦ SILVERSEA'S EXCLUSIVE PROVIDER

Special Needs Group (SNG) / Special Needs at Sea

🌐 specialneedsatsea.com <https://www.specialneedsatsea.com>

📋 *Equipment:* Scooters, wheelchairs, powerchairs, plus medical equipment
(oxygen, CPAP, shower chairs)

🚢 *Delivery:* Direct to your cabin, worldwide

⏱ *Booking:* Recommend reserving at least 3 weeks before sailing

💰 *Pricing:* Approximately $35–$80/day for scooters (multi-day discounts
available)

SNG is Silversea's *exclusive* mobility equipment partner, so they're fully
integrated with the ship's accessibility team and familiar with the Silver
Nova's layout.

ALSO AVAILABLE

Scootaround

🌐 scootaround.com <https://www.scootaround.com>

The largest cruise-specific rental network — services most major lines
including Silversea. A solid alternative with comparable pricing
(~$30–$75/day).

A couple of things worth noting:

   - If you think you might want a scooter onboard, it's worth flagging
   that early — *accessible cabins are limited* and book quickly.
   - Most providers offer a *damage waiver*, and your travel insurance may
   also cover rental equipment.
   - For port excursions in Japan, both providers can arrange equipment at
   select ports of call.

This is simply for your awareness — no action needed right now. But if
you'd like me to look into this further or help you reserve anything, I'm
happy to take care of it.

And as always — John personally oversees every detail of your trip, so
you're in the best hands.

examples.subject: Re: What Organized Travel Actually Looks Like
examples.body: Hi Missy, Following up on the seat assignments for your outbound flights — I promised I'd come back to you, and here's where we are. What We Did John and I researched Finnair's seat selection policies for your Business Class flights and attempted to secure specific seats on your behalf. Because your booking originates through American Airlines (AA confirmation CKZHXA) but the flights are operated by Finnair (confirmation BB4X94), seat selection has to be done directly through Finnair's system — AA's system can't assign seats on Finnair-operated flights in advance. What's Available Your Business Class is fully guaranteed on both legs — that hasn't changed. Finnair flies the A350 on the DFW–Helsinki route, which has a 1-2-1 Business Class layout — every seat has direct aisle access. These are excellent seats no matter where you end up, but if you have a preference (window-side, certain row), you can lock that in now. How to Select Your Seats — Step by Step It takes about 3 minutes: 1. Go to finnair.com and click "Manage booking" (top right) 2. Enter your Finnair confirmation code: BB4X94 3. Enter last name: FURLOW 4. Once you're in, look for "Seat selection" or "Choose seats" 5. You'll see the seat map for each flight: — Aug 26: AA 9018 (Finnair operated) DFW → Helsinki — Aug 27: AY 811 Helsinki → Stockholm 6. Pick two seats for each leg (one for you, one for John) 7. Confirm your selections A few tips: - Business Class seat selection on Finnair is typically included at no extra charge for your fare class - On the A350, rows 1–6 are Business Class in a 1-2-1 "throne" configuration — window seats (A and K) offer the most privacy, middle pairs (D and G) are great for couples who want to be next to each other - If prompted for any fees, stop and let me know — that would mean the system is reading the fare class differently and I'll sort it out If you'd prefer not to deal with it, no problem at all — just let me know and John and I will find another way to get it done. We wanted to give you the option since it's quick and you'll get first pick of whatever's open. I have notified John, he is aware and he and I will be working the problem. Looking forward to connecting with you! Dani — Dani Moreau Luxury Travel Concierge Dreams2Memories Travel concierge@d2mluxury.quest

DREAMS2MEMORIES

Curating the Voyage of Your Lifetime

Hi Ron,

I hope this message finds you well! I wanted to share a resource that may
be useful as you and Lindy prepare for your *Silversea Silver Nova* voyage
to Japan this April.

Whether you're planning ahead or just want to know your options, there are
dedicated mobility scooter and wheelchair rental services that work
directly with cruise lines — including Silversea. They handle everything:
delivery to your cabin, embarkation and debarkation logistics, and even
availability at select ports of call.

✦ SILVERSEA'S EXCLUSIVE PROVIDER

Special Needs Group (SNG) / Special Needs at Sea

🌐 specialneedsatsea.com <https://www.specialneedsatsea.com>

📋 *Equipment:* Scooters, wheelchairs, powerchairs, plus medical equipment
(oxygen, CPAP, shower chairs)

🚢 *Delivery:* Direct to your cabin, worldwide

⏱ *Booking:* Recommend reserving at least 3 weeks before sailing

💰 *Pricing:* Approximately $35–$80/day for scooters (multi-day discounts
available)

SNG is Silversea's *exclusive* mobility equipment partner, so they're fully
integrated with the ship's accessibility team and familiar with the Silver
Nova's layout.

ALSO AVAILABLE

Scootaround

🌐 scootaround.com <https://www.scootaround.com>

The largest cruise-specific rental network — services most major lines
including Silversea. A solid alternative with comparable pricing
(~$30–$75/day).

A couple of things worth noting:

   - If you think you might want a scooter onboard, it's worth flagging
   that early — *accessible cabins are limited* and book quickly.
   - Most providers offer a *damage waiver*, and your travel insurance may
   also cover rental equipment.
   - For port excursions in Japan, both providers can arrange equipment at
   select ports of call.

This is simply for your awareness — no action needed right now. But if
you'd like me to look into this further or help you reserve anything, I'm
happy to take care of it.

examples.subject: WHat do you guys think of this itinerary?
examples.body:
Hi guys, I asked my AI staff to suggest a romantic Saturday drive, they
came up with this. Any thoughts?

John

🌊 The Laguna Coast Romantic Drive (10:00 AM – 4:00 PM)

10:00 AM — Depart the Marriott & Hit PCH

   - Head south from the hotel toward the coast and catch the Pacific Coast
   Highway (PCH / Hwy 1) heading south through Corona del Mar.
   - *The Drive:* Once you pass Corona del Mar, the landscape opens up into
   rolling coastal hills on your left and the vast Pacific on your right. Roll
   the windows down—it’s a stunning stretch of road.

10:30 AM — Morning Stroll at Crystal Cove

   - Stop: Crystal Cove State Park Historic District.
   - Park in the Los Trancos lot (across PCH) and take the $2 shuttle (or a
   quick walk) down to the beach. This is a beautifully preserved slice of
   1930s coastal California with vintage beach cottages right on the sand.
   It’s incredibly romantic and a great spot for a morning photo.

11:45 AM — Drive into Laguna Beach & Crescent Bay Point

   - Continue south on PCH into Laguna Beach.
   - Quick Detour: Turn right onto Crescent Bay Drive and park near Crescent
   Bay Point Park. It’s a tiny, hidden panoramic park perched on a cliff
   looking down at the coves and crashing waves. Often very quiet and
   breathtaking.

12:30 PM — A Romantic Oceanfront Lunch
Laguna Beach is famous for restaurants perched directly over the surf. Here
are the top three romantic options (I highly recommend making a reservation
in advance for a Saturday!):

   1. Splashes (at the Surf & Sand Resort): You are seated literally 25
   feet above the crashing waves. If the tide is high, the ocean spray
   sometimes hits the glass. Incredible Mediterranean/Californian food.
   2. The Deck on Laguna Beach: A bit more casual but still highly
   romantic. It is built on the sand, offering fantastic seafood, oysters, and
   great cocktails with an unobstructed view of the horizon.
   3. Las Brisas: A Laguna classic perched on the cliff above Heisler Park.
   They serve upscale coastal Mexican cuisine with a legendary view of the
   coastline.

2:30 PM — Post-Lunch: Heisler Park or Art Galleries

   - If you eat at Las Brisas, simply walk out the front door into Heisler
   Park. It’s a paved, cliffside walking path lined with flowers,
   sculptures, and tide pools below.
   - Alternatively, wander through the downtown Laguna village to pop into
   a few of the famous local art galleries.

3:15 PM — The Drive Back via Shady Canyon

   - Instead of taking PCH back the exact same way, head inland on CA-133
   North through the Laguna Canyon. The canyon road is winding, shaded by
   eucalyptus trees, and offers a completely different, rustic California vibe.
   - Connect to the 73 North (toll road, but very fast and scenic) which
   will drop you right back by the Marriott Bayview.

4:00 PM — Arrive back at the Bayview Marriott

examples.subject: TESS Travel Agent 0Auths and client credentials
examples.body:
Hi Caitlin,

I'm John Loucks — I run Dreams2Memories Travel, a luxury cruise and travel
agency hosted with Outside Agents. I've been using TESS and Odysseus for
client and booking management, and I have to say, the platform is very
solid.

 Here's why I'm reaching out: I've built an extensive operations system
that includes automated trip dossiers for clients, commission
tracking,  payment
deadline alerts, cruise trip component research, and similar tasks. Right
now I'm manually copying data between TESS and my tools, which works but
it's slow and error-prone. What I'd love to do is connect them directly
through the TESS API so the data flows automatically.  I did try to put in
a ticket with MAGSOS but at the end of the conversation, there was no way
to create one. So, I tried again a few hours later with thee same result.
The I tried MAGGE, but she was unable assist.  So, I chose you from the org
list--may be right, may be wrong.  But...if you are the right person to
chat with, please read on, if not, can you pass me to the right person?

 Specifically, I'm looking to:

 - Pull my MAGCRM booking, trip, communication, and client data into my trip
dossier system so clients get polished, up-to-date travel documents
 - Track commission status without logging in and checking manually
 - Monitor the client's inputs t their portal

 - Sync payment deadlines into my alert system so nothing slips through the
cracks
 - Eventually push documents (proposals, itineraries, guides) back into
client trips

 I've already built the integration on my side — OAuth 2.0 with PKCE,
following the authentication pattern from your documentation. It's a
local desktop
application, single-agent use, just for my own agency data. All I need to
get it connected are OAuth client credentials (a client_id and
client_secret).

 I'm happy to start with read-only access and earn my way to write access
once you're comfortable with how I'm using it. No bulk operations, no
scraping, no sharing data outside my agency — just trying to run a tighter
ship.

 Would love to chat about it if that's easier — I'm pretty flexible on
timing. And if there's a formal process or application I should go through
nstead, just point me in the right direction.

 Thanks for your time, and thanks for building an API worth integrating
with.

John A Loucks III
Owner, Dreams2Memories, LLC

examples.subject: TESS Travel Agent 0Auths and client credentials
examples.body:
Hi Caitlin,

I'm John Loucks — I run Dreams2Memories Travel, a luxury cruise and travel
agency hosted with Outside Agents. I've been using TESS and Odysseus for
client and booking management, and I have to say, the platform is very
solid.

 Here's why I'm reaching out: I've built an extensive operations system
that includes automated trip dossiers for clients, commission
tracking,  payment
deadline alerts, cruise trip component research, and similar tasks. Right
now I'm manually copying data between TESS and my tools, which works but
it's slow and error-prone. What I'd love to do is connect them directly
through the TESS API so the data flows automatically.  I did try to put in
a ticket with MAGSOS but at the end of the conversation, there was no way
to create one. So, I tried again a few hours later with thee same result.
The I tried MAGGE, but she was unable assist.  So, I chose you from the org
list--may be right, may be wrong.  But...if you are the right person to
chat with, please read on, if not, can you pass me to the right person?

 Specifically, I'm looking to:

 - Pull my MAGCRM booking, trip, communication, and client data into my trip
dossier system so clients get polished, up-to-date travel documents
 - Track commission status without logging in and checking manually
 - Monitor the client's inputs t their portal

 - Sync payment deadlines into my alert system so nothing slips through the
cracks
 - Eventually push documents (proposals, itineraries, guides) back into
client trips

 I've already built the integration on my side — OAuth 2.0 with PKCE,
following the authentication pattern from your documentation. It's a
local desktop
application, single-agent use, just for my own agency data. All I need to
get it connected are OAuth client credentials (a client_id and
client_secret).

 I'm happy to start with read-only access and earn my way to write access
once you're comfortable with how I'm using it. No bulk operations, no
scraping, no sharing data outside my agency — just trying to run a tighter
ship.

 Would love to chat about it if that's easier — I'm pretty flexible on
timing. And if there's a formal process or application I should go through
nstead, just point me in the right direction.

 Thanks for your time, and thanks for building an API worth integrating
with.

John A Loucks III
Owner, Dreams2Memories, LLC

drilled straight into a power wire supplying an outlet. See the pictures
again.  You can see his 1st hole and the wire visible in the recesses.  He

optic cable cap while researching the problem, he discovered 2 holes and
the ensuing cable damage.  $1,400 later, the outlet is repaired. I would
like you to repay me with credit for the entire cost.  The outlet was
clearly working before the tech nicked the power wire.  You can even pay me
back with service credits.  But please pay the charge. I have all the

examples.subject: Our Kyoto & Mt. Fuji Adventure — April 21-22
examples.body:
Loucks_Japan_Kyoto_Fuji_Apr2026.html
<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jOtqzPpSLFhgtYVFDSmxpoBCB-uzQ7n1/view?usp=drive_web>
Hey Susie!

I put together a plan for our two free days in Japan and I think you're
going to love it.

April 21st — we hop on the bullet train to Kyoto (it's only 2 hours!). A
guide walks us through Nishiki Market in the morning — think grilled
skewers, matcha sweets, and all kinds of street food. Then we grab lunch at
Katsukura, which is supposed to be THE best tonkatsu in Kyoto. Afternoon we
have a private car that takes us through the bamboo groves and past the
temples — we can hop out to shop or just enjoy the views from the car. Back
on the bullet train by 7pm.

April 22nd — a private car picks us up right at the hotel and drives us to
Mt. Fuji and Hakone for the day. Cable cars, lake views, volcanic hot
springs, and these famous black eggs that supposedly add 7 years to your
life (we'll need a few of those). Everything is flat and easy — no hiking,
lots of sitting and snacking.

No raw fish anywhere. Plenty of katsu. And we set the pace the whole time.

The whole thing is about $1,241 for both of us ($621 each) including
trains, taxis, tours, and lunches. I attached the full proposal with all
the details.

Should be fun! Take a look and let me know what you think.

Love,
John

examples.subject: Our Kyoto & Mt. Fuji Adventure — April 21-22
examples.body:
Loucks_Japan_Kyoto_Fuji_Apr2026.html
<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jOtqzPpSLFhgtYVFDSmxpoBCB-uzQ7n1/view?usp=drive_web>
Hey Susie!

I put together a plan for our two free days in Japan and I think you're
going to love it.

April 21st — we hop on the bullet train to Kyoto (it's only 2 hours!). A
guide walks us through Nishiki Market in the morning — think grilled
skewers, matcha sweets, and all kinds of street food. Then we grab lunch at
Katsukura, which is supposed to be THE best tonkatsu in Kyoto. Afternoon we
have a private car that takes us through the bamboo groves and past the
temples — we can hop out to shop or just enjoy the views from the car. Back
on the bullet train by 7pm.

April 22nd — a private car picks us up right at the hotel and drives us to
Mt. Fuji and Hakone for the day. Cable cars, lake views, volcanic hot
springs, and these famous black eggs that supposedly add 7 years to your
life (we'll need a few of those). Everything is flat and easy — no hiking,
lots of sitting and snacking.

No raw fish anywhere. Plenty of katsu. And we set the pace the whole time.

The whole thing is about $1,241 for both of us ($621 each) including
trains, taxis, tours, and lunches. I attached the full proposal with all
the details.

Should be fun! Take a look and let me know what you think.

Love,
John
